properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live SSH invocations in the cluster deployment/network scripts (net/common.sh, colo-provider.sh, colo-utils.sh, create-solana-user.sh, ec2-provider.sh) that disable host-key verification: the ssh/scp tunnels to cluster nodes authenticate nothing. Posture control — changeable here by pinning known host keys or enabling StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the sha1@0.10.5 crate is what the build resolves — SHA-1 ships in the resulting binaries whether or not first-party code calls it (reachability through transitive deps cannot be excluded from a lockfile). Confirming presence; the call-site question is the finding layer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is Solana's foundational signature scheme — every transaction, vote, shred (ledger/src/sigverify_shreds.rs ed25519_verify_many/sign_many) and the Ed25519SigVerify111... precompile. ed25519-dalek is pinned EXACTLY at =1.0.1 (Cargo.toml:197) because verification is consensus-critical: the version is frozen by protocol compatibility, so library fixes (including the 1.0.x dalek CVE/behavior changes) cannot be taken without a feature gate. Keygen: Keypair::generate(&mut OsRng) (keypair.rs:36)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA genuinely used for CI/cluster SSH access: ssh-keygen -t ecdsa generates the buildkite agent's key (setup-buildkite.sh:47) and 15 ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 public keys are committed as authorized_keys material for cluster nodes (net/scripts/solana-user-authorized_keys.sh). The 4 perf/ledger debug-string sites were rejected as Ed25519 mislabels. Changeable here — regenerate as Ed25519 (used elsewhere in this repo) or plan ML-DSA once OpenSSH ships it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: These 15 sites are the NIST P-256 curve of the same committed SSH public keys — real access-granting key material for cluster nodes. Same key material as ALG-710f61f0's authorized_keys sites, recorded here as the curve attribute.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: ed25519-dalek@1.0.1 is resolved in Cargo.lock — an Ed25519 implementation ships in the build (the ledger's consensus signature algorithm is Ed25519; this crate is part of that supply chain). Version 1.0.1 is the legacy line; the repo also resolves newer dalek versions elsewhere.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live curl invocations in the CI image build and agent setup pin --tlsv1.2 (minimum TLS 1.2) for downloading rustup from sh.rustup.rs. TLS 1.2 negotiates classical ECDHE key exchange — harvestable. A floor rather than a cap; actual version decided by the server. Changeable here only up to what rustup's endpoints negotiate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: curve25519-dalek@3.2.1 (Curve25519/Edwards arithmetic) is resolved in Cargo.lock — ships in the build. Curve25519 group operations underpin the repo's X25519/Ed25519 usage; Shor-vulnerable group.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: X25519 arrives via ring@0.16.20 in Cargo.lock. ring 0.16.20 is an old release; its X25519/ECDH and TLS stack are quantum-vulnerable and the pinned version constrains any later PQ-group adoption. Confirming presence; ring here is likely transitive (rustls/native-tls ecosystem).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256/SHA3-512 usage across Solana: BPF syscall sol_keccak256 (bpf_loader/syscalls/mod.rs:317, sdk keccak.rs, C headers keccak.h), Ethereum-style address derivation in secp256k1_instruction.rs:852/911/999, and SHA3-512 hash-to-scalar/point for zk-token ElGamal/Pedersen commitments. Quantum-safe hashes. All 44 sites in 17 files seen and genuine.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 is genuinely and pervasively in use: account/pubkey hashing in accounts-db (blake3::hash, blake3::Hasher), the sol_blake3 BPF syscall exposed to on-chain programs (bpf_loader syscalls + Blake3Hasher, sdk/program/src/blake3.rs wrapper, C SDK headers, feature-gated blake3_syscall_enabled), transaction message hashing (sdk/program/src/message/legacy.rs:481, versions/mod.rs:148), plus the sbf C/Rust demo programs. Hash primitive — Grover-only, not Shor-vulnerable. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM-SIV is the real authenticated-encryption primitive of the zk-token confidential-transfer design: zk-token-sdk/src/encryption/auth_encryption.rs instantiates Aes128GcmSiv (new/encrypt/decrypt at lines 77 and 93), and zk-keygen generates and recovers the AES128 keys (seed-phrase derived) that programs use to encrypt ElGamal ciphertexts. Symmetric, Grover-only; below CNSA 2.0's AES-256 preference but 128-bit remains the ecosystem default. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with 2048 rounds (keypair.rs:246-255, salt "mnemonic"+passphrase) derives BIP39 seed phrases into wallet keypair seeds — the 2048 count is the BIP39 standard, fixed by ecosystem compatibility (replaceable only by the wallet standard, not here), but far below OWASP's 210k minimum for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 (CWE-916). Dependency declarations at Cargo.toml:261, sdk/Cargo.toml:65, Cargo.lock.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM-SIV (aes-gcm-siv crate, not plain GCM): the AEAD protecting zk-token AuthCiphertext — encrypt at auth_encryption.rs:77, decrypt at :93, import at :9, crate in Cargo.lock. 128-bit key gives 64-bit effective security under Grover; migration is an AES-256 variant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE-256 XOF (Keccak, quantum-safe) used to derive Bulletproofs-style Pedersen generators in zk-token-sdk range proofs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac@0.8.1 in the Cargo.lock build graph — dependency-inventory entry; HMAC is symmetric and quantum-resistant in practice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.3.1 in docs/package-lock.json brings a pure-JS AES implementation into the docs-site build. Presence confirmed; use is the finding layer's question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: sha2@0.9.9 (SHA-256/SHA-512) is resolved in Cargo.lock — SHA-256 is the hash under most of the repo's hashing (hashes are Groestl/SHA-256 in solana). SHA-256 is not Shor-vulnerable (Grover halves it only), but it is part of the inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3@1.5.0 in the build graph — Solana uses BLAKE3 for account-state hashing; symmetric, quantum-safe.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OsRng (operating-system CSPRNG) supplies randomness for zk-token proof blinding (sigma proofs, range proofs, ElGamal encryption) via 9 import sites in zk-token-sdk — quantum-safe and appropriate. The one false site (tempfile rand_bytes(0)) was rejected separately.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek is THE signature library of this codebase — solana's consensus signatures (sdk/src/signature.rs) are Ed25519 over ed25519-dalek, and the crate is resolved in Cargo.lock. Every validator transaction and shred signature flows through it. Shor-vulnerable; migration is ML-DSA (FIPS 204) once the chain's signature scheme can change — a protocol-level decision, not a library swap.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: openssl 0.10.64 (Rust bindings) enters via goauth 0.13.1/smpl_jwt 0.7.1 for the GCP BigTable OAuth path (storage-bigtable) and is VENDORED — built statically via the "vendored" feature (storage-bigtable/Cargo.toml:39-47) — so the OpenSSL version (3.x, classical KX/RSA only) is pinned at build time by openssl-src, not by the host OS. Supplies the RSA RS256 JWT signing and TLS for the BigTable gRPC/HTTPS session; PQ capability is decided by the vendored 3.x line (no ML-KEM hybrid support).

properties.value: The openssl crate (bindings to the system OpenSSL) is resolved at 0.10.64 in Cargo.lock — likely via native-tls/reqwest in the validator's outbound HTTP paths. Post-quantum capability is decided by the OpenSSL library linked at runtime, which the crate version only loosely bounds; recorded so the supply chain is visible when PQ groups (X25519MLKEM768 in OpenSSL 3.5+) are planned.

properties.name: pqs:context

Its ECDHE key exchange is harvestable (harvest-now-decrypt-later); upgrading native-tls/OpenSSL is what eventually enables hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 groups. Recorded for the transport-migration plan.
